Will you report to the police?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'at' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('I have') (possession) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('from (ask from someone)') (просить у кого) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
He's at our place.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: As you all know...
Does the governor support you?

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'дрыв'). Common masculine noun meaning 'strain, anguish' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You have a partial ligament tear.

examples.text: Врач сказал, что у вас небольшой надрыв связок.
examples.trans: The doctor said that you have a slight ligament tear.

examples.text: Она говорила об этом с настоящим душевным надрывом.
examples.trans: She spoke about it with real emotional anguish.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'вязка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'ligament, vocal cord' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You have a partial ligament tear.
Over and out.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.
It's very hard.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'scary'.

examples.trans: I got scared.
Did you really suddenly get scared?

examples.text: Он ночью страшно и громко храпит!
examples.trans: At night he snores terribly and loudly!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'гружать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'load, burden'.

examples.trans: Keep your weight off that leg.

examples.text: Врач сказал пока сильно не нагружать больную ногу.
examples.trans: The doctor said not to put much weight on the injured leg for now.

examples.text: Не надо нагружать нового повара всеми заказами сразу.
examples.trans: Do not overload the new cook with all the orders at once.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'leg', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('foot') (Russian uses one word for both) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The right foot.
My leg hurts.

examples.text: Заходите. Поставьте, пожалуйста, правую ногу на кровать.
examples.trans: Come in. Please put your right foot on the bed.

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.trans: Thanks, Dad!
Thank you for your trust!

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('what') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.trans: What is your town like?
What a beautiful house!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'чина'). Common feminine noun meaning 'reason, cause' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Нет причин держать вас под арестом.
examples.trans: There is no reason to keep you under arrest.
What is the reason?

examples.text: Нет причин держать вас под арестом. Сегодня вы выйдете отсюда.
examples.trans: There is no reason to keep you under arrest. Today you will walk out of here.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('your') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.trans: Who are your rivals?
Is this your programme?
Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'injury, trauma' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: What is the cause of your injury?

examples.text: А трава в мешках сгорела. Из-за вас!
examples.trans: And the herbs in the sacks burned. Because of you!

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пасть'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to hit', forming an aspectual pair with 'попадать'.

meanings.en: to get to, to end up
meanings.note: как попасть в центр? = how do I get to the centre?

examples.trans: A firework hit the power station.
How do I get to the station?

examples.text: Скажи: салют попал в станцию. Три района без света.
examples.trans: Say a firework hit the power station. Three districts without electricity.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'under' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('under (towards)') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('on (someone's responsibility)') (под мою ответственность) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The cat is under the table.
On my responsibility.

examples.text: Хорошо, давайте три. Под мою личную ответственность.
examples.trans: All right, let's say three. On my personal responsibility.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'car; machine' in everyday Russian.
Secondary conversational sense ('machine') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Is this our car now?
Which car did you come in?
A car. A German one.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'являть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to declare'.

examples.trans: I am reporting it stolen.
Will you report to the police?
I will not report it.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Borrowed in the Petrine era from German 'Polizei' / French 'police' (from Greek 'politeia', civil administration).

examples.trans: Call the police!
The police are here.

examples.text: Тут кнопки вызова: скорая, полиция и мы.
examples.trans: Here are the call buttons: ambulance, police, and us.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
Secondary conversational sense ('there isn't') (+ genitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: No, it's mine.
No? All right.
No. That's mine.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'быть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forget', paired with 'забывать'.

examples.trans: Don't forget to wash the toilet.
I forgot the keys.

examples.text: Сейчас будешь чинить трубу. И унитаз не забудь помыть.
examples.trans: Now you're going to fix the pipe. And don't forget to wash the toilet.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ставить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to put', forming an aspectual pair with 'ставить'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to install') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Put your foot on the bed.
Put the cup here.

examples.text: Заходите. Поставьте, пожалуйста, правую ногу на кровать.
examples.trans: Come in. Please put your right foot on the bed.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'handbrake' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я забыл поставить машину на ручник.
examples.trans: I forgot to put the car on handbrake.

examples.text: Я в спешке совсем забыл поставить машину на ручник.
examples.trans: In my hurry I completely forgot to put the car on the handbrake.

examples.text: На крутом склоне всегда проверяй, держит ли ручник.
examples.trans: On a steep slope always check whether the handbrake holds.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('she') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.trans: She's a lecturer.
I haven't heard of her.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'confront, run into'.

examples.trans: And it ran over me.

examples.text: Водитель не заметил знак и случайно наехал на бордюр.
examples.trans: The driver did not notice the sign and accidentally ran into the curb.

examples.text: Почему шеф с самого утра так строго наехал на нас?
examples.trans: Why did the chef come down so hard on us first thing in the morning?

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'clear'.
Secondary conversational sense ('I see') (as a reply) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: All clear.
I see, thanks.
I'm going to be mayor, understood?
